analysis_subset.rule: species with all five frozen folds evaluable, so full species-by-island observed state can be reconstructed from the already-open authoritative held-out artifact without opening any new response source

feature_reconstruction.geometry_source: frozen 842-island coordinates from the pre-outcome isolation-contract artifact
feature_reconstruction.component_rule: exact source-code rule: undirected component under haversine distance <= radius
feature_reconstruction.species_sources: outer-training presences only for each frozen fold
feature_reconstruction.generic_mainland_step_frequency: fraction of radii whose focal component contains an island within that radius of continental Australia
feature_reconstruction.species_conditioned_eog_frequency: fraction of radii whose focal component contains an outer-training presence of the focal species

E11_species_specific_excess_connectivity.interpretation: Every excess-connectivity row is connected to an occupied species source at all four frozen radii while generic mainland access fails at the smallest 25-km radius. This is a predictor-only signature of insular-source connectivity exceeding generic mainland stepping.

E12_remote_presence_alignment.question: Within remote islands, does predictor-only excess source connectivity mark the presence rows where adding species-conditioned topology is helpful rather than harmful?
E12_remote_presence_alignment.interpretation: The remote-tail regime switch is concentrated in rows where species-conditioned source connectivity exceeds generic mainland stepping. This is post-outcome alignment evidence, not a causal colonization estimate.

E13_multihop_stepping_stone_state.definition: species-conditioned connectivity is present at the 25-km graph but nearest occupied training source is farther than 25 km; therefore connectivity requires at least one intermediate island under the frozen graph
E13_multihop_stepping_stone_state.interpretation: Species-conditioned topology can encode a source path that nearest-source distance alone does not represent: a focal island may be more than 25 km from any occupied source yet remain in the source component through a chain of <=25-km inter-island links.

E14_mechanistic_reframing.previous_hypothesis: extreme isolation causes topology to re-emerge
E14_mechanistic_reframing.refined_hypothesis: extreme isolation creates the opportunity for species-conditioned insular source paths to diverge from generic mainland connectivity; topology is informative when it represents those source-specific multi-hop paths rather than generic remoteness itself
E14_mechanistic_reframing.why_remote_tail_still_matters: species-specific EOG can exceed generic mainland stepping only in the remote tail of the reconstructed five-fold-evaluable data
E14_mechanistic_reframing.why_remoteness_is_not_sufficient: multi-hop source-connected presence rows can be favourable outside the remote tail as well; remoteness is therefore a context enabling source/generic decoupling, not the sole mechanism

updated_ecological_synthesis: Area, mainland distance and direct source proximity absorb much of the structural signal under ordinary island conditions.
The residual topology signal is best understood as source-conditioned path information rather than generic network position.
A biologically distinctive state occurs when an island remains connected to occupied insular sources at scales where generic mainland stepping is already broken.
Multi-hop inter-island paths can make species-conditioned topology informative even when the nearest occupied source is farther than the smallest graph radius.

The remote-tail regime switch is therefore reframed as insular-source decoupling: remote islands can be disconnected from generic mainland entry yet remain connected to the focal species' occupied archipelago source network.
This does not establish colonization, rescue effects, persistence, or realized movement; those remain prospective biological mechanisms.
claim_ceiling: do not call excess connectivity a colonization probability
do not infer realized stepping-stone movement from graph paths
do not claim that the 25-km scale is biologically universal
do not claim remote islands are maintained by rescue effects from these analyses
do not promote true-presence subgroup diagnostics into the frozen primary result
do not treat the 687-species reconstruction subset as a new confirmatory denominator
do not change the frozen 75%-tail future primary using v0.3 subgroup results
